title: Deployment lifecycle staircase proposal
body:
Purpose:
Short internal proposal for how we stage a customer POC through a three-step deployment lifecycle (hosted -> dedicated -> private) while keeping risk low and operational overhead predictable. Target audience: solutions engineers + customer SREs + account lead.

Executive summary:
We recommend a staircase approach: start in Hosted (fastest time-to-value), graduate to Dedicated for predictable throughput & data isolation when steady-state traffic emerges, and only move to Private for regulatory/data-sovereignty or network-isolation requirements. Each stair has gated exit criteria, automated migration artifacts, and explicit rollback paths. This minimizes customer friction and shortens time to measurable results.

Key principles:
- Gate on metrics not calendar: only advance when latency, error-rate, and cost per token stabilize within agreed tolerances.
- Preserve API parity: keep same route and prompt semantics across all modes; let routing/policy layer handle variant mapping.
- Reduce migration blast radius: use canary slices and prefix-KV cache warmups.
- Measurable economics: provide a simple per-100k request cost delta estimate for each transition.

Stair definitions and what changes:
1) Hosted (POC stage)
  - Billing: standard usage-based.
  - Config: latest curated open model, default batching.
  - Ops: Redwood manages runtime; we instrument SLO dashboards and enable token-level cost breakdown.
  - Customer ask: quick eval, function calling, small test datasets.
2) Dedicated (onboarding stage)
  - Billing: reserved capacity + metered burst.
  - Config: pinned model version, fine-tuned autoscaling policy, explicit batch sizing.
  - Ops: shared runbook with customer SRE; increased retention for traces.
  - Customer ask: predictable latency, SLA negotiation.
3) Private (production/regulatory stage)
  - Billing: platform fee + infra; enterprise license.
  - Config: VPC peering or on-prem package, KMS/HSM integration, audit logging.
  - Ops: joint runbook + support rotation; stricter change control.
  - Customer ask: full data sovereignty, air-gapped where required.

Exit criteria (example gating checklist) — must satisfy all to progress:
- 7-day rolling p95 latency within target (e.g., < 500ms for chat path)
- Error rate < 0.5% (5xx and model-timeouts)
- Cost delta projection for next 30d within budget threshold (<20% increase)
- Key eval prompts show no quality regression (automated eval harness green)
- Customer ops sign-off (SRE/Platform)

Migration mechanics (practical steps)
- Pre-migration: capture current model config, temperature/scoring, and batch profiles. Take snapshot of KV cache access patterns.
- Warm-up: synthetic traffic that mirrors 20% production token distribution to warm embeddings and KV caches on destination nodes.
- Traffic slicing: 1% canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on SLA breach.
- Database & logs: ensure log forwarding to customer's SIEM during dedicated stage; escalate to private retention policy only when on prem.
- Rollback: keep consumer-level feature flags to redirect to previous environment within 60s.

Observability & quality gates:
- Baseline dashboards: per-route latency heatmap, token-cost trend, model perplexity/response-length distribution.
- Prompt set evals: run nightly regression checks against golden prompts after each change.
- Alerting: SLO breaches to Redwood SRE + customer Slack channel + PagerDuty for dedicated/private.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Hosted: recommend data redaction at ingress and customer tokenization for sensitive fields.
- Dedicated: KMS on dedicated nodes, RBAC for API keys, audit logs retained per contract.
- Private: HSM integration, VPC peering-only management plane access, formal SOC2/ISO attestation attachment.

Estimated timeline (typical POC -> private path)
- Hosted POC: 1–2 weeks (integration + validation)
- Dedicated onboarding: 2–4 weeks (capacity sizing + SLA setup + runbooks)
- Private deployment: 4–8 weeks (networking + security + legal sign-offs)
Total (fast path): ~7–14 weeks depending on procurement and customer network complexity.

Rough cost delta examples (order-of-magnitude for discussion)
- Hosted baseline: $0.10 per 1k tokens (example only)
- Dedicated amortized: platform + reserved GPU = +30–50% unit cost but lower variance and predictable spend
- Private on-prem: initial setup large fixed cost; per-token marginal cost lowest at scale but long payback window

Failure modes and mitigations (unique points)
- Cache divergence: KV caches may warm differently -> mitigation: compare response fingerprints for golden prompts during warm-up and pause if mismatch.
- Model variant drift after pinning: run nightly lightweight evals and allow fast rollback to previous model.bin if regression detected.
- Network flaps during private cutover: use traffic mirror + blackhole detection + holdback on DNS TTL change.

Customer-facing artifacts we should prepare:
- One-page "Staircase migration checklist" for their SRE (PDF)
- Canister script for automated warm-up traffic (GitHub)
- Cost comparison spreadsheet (sheet) with sample usage buckets
- Runbook template (doc) for canary and rollback steps

Open questions / asks for sales/legal/infra:
- Legal: acceptable retention windows for logs in dedicated vs private? (Need bullet list from legal)
- Sales: what discounting floor applies when a customer moves from hosted to dedicated reserved capacity?
- Infra: can we provide a certified deployment template for two popular on-prem vendors (Dell, Supermicro)?

Next steps (short-term)
- Share with account lead and schedule a 30-min runbook walkthrough with customer SRE (owner: Miguel) - target by 2025-03-07
- Prep the canary warm-up script and cost sheet (owner: Priya) - target by 2025-03-05
- Legal to confirm log retention/PII handling options (owner: Jonah) - request by 2025-03-10

Notes to self / rough scribbles:
- Try a lightweight policy: automatic fallback to smaller model if p50 > 1s for > 10m window.
- Consider offering a migration credit for first month of dedicated reserved capacity to reduce friction.

End of doc.
